import pandas as pd
t = tables['trips']
t = t[t['fished_date_season']==1]  # season 1 only (should be all of it)

# per-day, per-class aggregate share = sum(yt)/sum(anglers)
g = t.groupby(['cls'])[['yt','anglers']].sum()
g['share'] = g['yt']/g['anglers']
g['n_trips'] = t.groupby('cls').size()

# by month (doy bucket ~30d)
t['month'] = (t['fished_date_doy']//30).astype(int)
gm = t.groupby('month')[['yt','anglers']].sum()
gm['share'] = gm['yt']/gm['anglers']
gm['n'] = t.groupby('month').size()

# overall zero-yt rate
zero_rate = (t.groupby(['fished_date_doy','cls'])['yt'].sum()==0).mean()

result = {'by_class': g.to_dict(), 'by_month': gm.to_dict(), 'zero_day_rate': zero_rate, 'doy_min': t['fished_date_doy'].min(), 'doy_max': t['fished_date_doy'].max()}

# Season 2 planning notes (written day 1, from season 1 full-season data)

## Bottom line
Yellowtail are essentially a longer-trip-only game. Half-day AM/PM and twilight trips are a
waste of money almost all season:
- hd_am share ≈0.009, hd_pm ≈0.010, hd_twilight ≈0.0, pooled over the whole season.
- Even in their best months (Apr-May) hd_am/hd_pm only hit ~0.03-0.06 share, and by June they're
  basically 0 through November.
=> Do not book HD_AM / HD_PM / TWILIGHT for yellowtail. Only use them if PTO/budget is otherwise idle
and another species matters (it doesn't for scoring), i.e. basically never.

The three classes that matter: THREE_QUARTER ($150), OVERNIGHT ($400), DAY_1_5 ($550).
Season-pooled share: three_quarter 0.242, overnight 0.419, day_1_5 0.457 (day_1_5/overnight also
included "multi_day" in raw class list but multi_day itself is NEVER offered/bookable - ignore it).
Season-pooled share-per-dollar: three_quarter 0.00161 > overnight 0.00105 > day_1_5 0.00083.
So three_quarter is the efficient default, but overnight/day_1_5 raise the ceiling on good windows.

## Seasonal timing (doy = day of year, buckets of 30 days, season 1 data)
Strong bimodal pattern - spring peak, summer trough, fall rebound:
- doy 90-119 (~April): three_quarter 0.51, overnight 1.48(!), day_1_5 2.21(n=7, thin)
- doy 120-149 (~May):  three_quarter 0.54, overnight 0.29, day_1_5 0.46(n=7, thin)
- doy 150-179 (~June): three_quarter 0.42, overnight 0.66, day_1_5 0.18
- doy 180-209 (~July):  three_quarter 0.06, overnight 0.01, day_1_5 0.01   <- TROUGH starts
- doy 210-239 (~Aug):   three_quarter 0.04, overnight 0.26, day_1_5 0.03
- doy 240-269 (~late Aug/Sep): three_quarter 0.02, overnight 0.06, day_1_5 0.04   <- TROUGH bottom
- doy 270-299 (~late Sep/Oct): three_quarter 0.30, overnight 0.64, day_1_5 2.16(n=69, solid)  <- FALL RUN
- doy 300-329 (~Nov):   three_quarter 0.07, overnight 0.20, day_1_5 2.01(n=5, thin)
- doy 330+ (~Dec):      basically 0 everywhere.

Read: April (doy90-119) and the Sep27-Oct26 window (doy270-299) are the two strongest windows across
every class, especially day_1_5 and overnight. July through most of September (doy180-269) is a real
trough - avoid committing PTO/budget there unless real-time signals (forecast, recent counts, fishdope
text) say otherwise. Caveat: several of the best numbers come from small n (7-15 trips) - trust the
live briefing's "recent counts" over these historical averages when they disagree, especially for
day_1_5 in April/Nov.

## Boats that stood out (n>=8 trips, overnight+day_1_5 pooled, season 1)
Prefer these when `ctx.scheduled_boats` lists them, over the naive `pick_boat` default:
Pacific Voyager (Seaforth, share 1.57), Cortez (Seaforth, 1.42), Ranger 85 (H&M, 1.28, n=29 - solid
sample), Top Gun 80 (H&M, 1.20), Constitution (H&M, 0.99), Grande (Point Loma, 0.83), Tomahawk
(Seaforth, 0.78, n=28 - solid), Mustang (H&M, 0.65, n=41 - solid sample). Ranger 85, Tomahawk and
Mustang have the most trips behind them so weight those most.

## Signals checked that did NOT help (season 1)
Daily fishdope numeric fields (migrated, yt_local, yt_all, wt_all) barely correlated with same-day
realized share across three_quarter/overnight/day_1_5 (all |corr| < 0.05, overlap sample was small).
Don't lean on the numeric fishdope columns alone - if using fishdope, read the narrative `text` field
directly at the nightly briefing rather than trusting the numeric summary fields.

## Budget/PTO plan for this season ($2000, 10 PTO)
Don't spend evenly across the season - concentrate on the two windows above.
Draft allocation to start from and adjust with live data:
- ~2 day_1_5 trips (1 in the April window, 1 in the Oct window) = $1100
- ~2 overnight trips (spread across April/June/Oct, whichever the live forecast favors) = $800
- Leaves ~$100 + a couple three_quarter trips as budget allows once real counts confirm a hot window.
- PTO discipline: PTO commits are irreversible and locked in 14 days ahead. Favor weekend/holiday
  departures for overnight and day_1_5 to save PTO days for when a weekday departure is clearly worth
  it (e.g. a strong forecast/recent-counts day inside the April or Oct window). Don't burn PTO in the
  Jul-Sep trough.
- Zero-day rate is high (~63% of class-days show zero yt across ALL classes pooled, historically) -
  variance is real even in good windows, so use the live briefing (recent boat counts, forecast, water
  temp trend) to pick the actual date/boat within a window, not just the calendar bucket.

## Open questions for next planning turn
- Once April arrives, check whether season 2's actual doy timing/ONI matches season 1's pattern before
  committing the bulk of PTO - season 1 is one sample, don't overfit to it if early live counts diverge.
- Check whether Scripps pier water temp (pier.wtmp_c) leads the fall run - didn't check yet, worth a
  quick correlation pass at the next planning turn if budget allows.
- Strategy.py is still a no-op ("no strategy yet"). Consider writing simple reflex code later (e.g.
  auto-commit PTO for weekend dates in the two hot windows) once nightly decisions have run a few times
  and the manual pattern is confirmed to work.
